Decision Curve Analysis for Right-Censored Survival Outcomes

Source: R/dca_survmat.R
dca_survmat.Rd

Computes net benefit across a range of risk thresholds at a fixed horizon t_star for a survival model's predicted risk, alongside the "treat all" and "treat none" reference strategies (Vickers and Elkin 2006), adapted to right-censored outcomes via the same inverse-probability-of- censoring weighting (IPCW) estimator of \(\hat G(t)\) used by brier and auc_survmat.

Usage

dca_survmat(object, predicted, t_star, thresholds = seq(0.01, 0.99, by = 0.01))

# S3 method for class 'dca_survmat'
plot(x, title, ...)

plot_dca(x, ...)

Arguments

object

A Surv object of length \(n\).

predicted

An n x k matrix or data frame of survival probabilities with columns named "t=<time>".

t_star

Numeric horizon at which risk is evaluated.

thresholds

Numeric vector of risk thresholds in (0, 1). Default seq(0.01, 0.99, by = 0.01).

x

A dca_survmat object.

title

Plot title. If missing, an automatically generated title is used. Pass NULL to omit the title entirely.

...

Additional arguments passed to plot.dca_survmat.

Value

An object of class "dca_survmat": a list with curve (a data.frame with threshold, model, treat_all, treat_none) and t_star.

Details

The predicted risk at the horizon is \(\pi_i = 1 - \hat S(t^\star \mid X_i)\). At threshold pt, subjects with \(\pi_i \ge pt\) are classified high-risk. Using the IPCW identity for the Kaplan-Meier estimator (Graf et al. 1999), the true- and false-positive fractions are estimated as $$ \widehat{\mathrm{TPF}}(pt) = \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n I(\pi_i \ge pt)\, \frac{\Delta_i\, I(\tilde T_i \le t^\star)}{\hat G(\tilde T_i)}, \qquad \widehat{\mathrm{FPF}}(pt) = \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n I(\pi_i \ge pt)\, \frac{I(\tilde T_i > t^\star)}{\hat G(t^\star)}, $$ and the net benefit is $$ \widehat{\mathrm{NB}}(pt) = \widehat{\mathrm{TPF}}(pt) - \widehat{\mathrm{FPF}}(pt) \cdot \frac{pt}{1-pt}. $$ "Treat all" (classify everyone high-risk) reduces to the marginal IPCW-KM identity \(1 - \hat S_{\mathrm{KM}}(t^\star)\) for the TPF term and \(\hat S_{\mathrm{KM}}(t^\star)\) for the FPF term. "Treat none" has net benefit \(0\) by definition.

References

Vickers AJ, Elkin EB (2006). "Decision Curve Analysis: A Novel Method for Evaluating Prediction Models." Medical Decision Making, 26(6), 565-574.

Vickers AJ, Van Calster B, Steyerberg EW (2019). "A Simple, Step-by-Step Guide to Interpreting Decision Curve Analysis." Diagnostic and Prognostic Research, 3, 18.

Graf E, Schmoor C, Sauerbrei W, Schumacher M (1999). "Assessment and Comparison of Prognostic Classification Schemes for Survival Data." Statistics in Medicine, 18(17-18), 2529-2545.

See also

plot.dca_survmat(), brier(), auc_survmat()

Examples

y <- survival::Surv(time = veteran$time, event = veteran$status)
sp <- matrix(stats::plogis(scale(veteran$karno)), ncol = 1,
            dimnames = list(NULL, "t=100"))
d <- dca_survmat(y, predicted = sp, t_star = 100)
head(d$curve)
#>   threshold     model  treat_all treat_none
#> 1      0.01 0.5781586 0.06430204          0
#> 2      0.02 0.5738541 0.05475410          0
#> 3      0.03 0.5694608 0.04500930          0
#> 4      0.04 0.5649760 0.03506148          0
#> 5      0.05 0.5603968 0.02490423          0
#> 6      0.06 0.5557202 0.01453087          0
